samples.summary: "the returned setup is a copy" test passes even if getPageSetup() returns the shared DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP by reference
samples.evidence: The test does `const setup = editor.getPageSetup(); setup.margins.top = 1; setup.paperSize.width = 1; expect(editor.getPageSetup()).toEqual(DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP)`. If `getPageSetup()` did NOT copy (e.g. returned `doc.document.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP`), the mutations would land on `DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` itself (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:745, whose `paperSize` is `PAPER_SIZES.LETTER` and whose `margins` is a shared literal), so the expected value would be mutated in lockstep with the actual and the assertion would still hold. The test therefore cannot fail for the exact aliasing bug it claims to guard. A meaningful version must compare against a frozen literal (`{paperSize:{name:'Letter',width:816,height:1056}, ...}`) or assert the returned object is not the same reference across two calls. Note it also mutates a module-level constant, which can leak into sibling tests.

samples.summary: No test exercises choosing a different paper size in the Page Setup dialog — the dialog's primary control
samples.evidence: Every test in docs-page-setup-dialog.test.tsx either seeds a paper size and asserts it round-trips unchanged ('seeds the orientation and paper size, and hands them back untouched', 'switches orientation without touching the paper size') or drives margins/orientation. Nothing ever fires the `Select`'s `onValueChange` (docs-page-setup-dialog.tsx: `onValueChange={(name) => { const next = PAPER_OPTIONS.find(...); if (next) setPaperSize(next); }}`), so a broken paper-size handler — user picks A4, document stays Letter — ships silently green. The `CUSTOM` sentinel branch (paper size matching no preset, rendered as `Custom (name)`) is likewise never rendered by any test. I grepped the frontend tests for `PAPER_SIZES`, `page-setup-paper`, `Paper size`, `A4` and read the whole dialog test file.
searchedFor: grep PAPER_SIZES / 'Paper size' / page-setup-paper in packages/frontend/tests

samples.summary: The format-painter toggle test does not pin the paste-before-clear ordering, so a reversed implementation would still pass
samples.evidence: 'applies to the selection and lets the format go on the second press' only asserts `pasteFormat` and `clearCopiedFormat` were each called once. If the component called `editor.clearCopiedFormat()` before `editor.pasteFormat()`, the real editor's `pasteFormat()` would find an empty buffer and write nothing (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:428 `if (!this.styleBuffer) return false;`) — the button would silently never paint — yet both call-count assertions and the `aria-pressed` assertion still hold (the stub's `pasteFormat` returns `held && selectionPresent`, and its return value is not checked in this test). Asserting `expect(editor.pasteFormat).toHaveReturnedWith(true)` (or `mock.invocationCallOrder`) would close it.

samples.summary: Nothing asserts that setPageSetup actually repaginates/relayouts — only that the value reaches the store
samples.evidence: `writePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:~2006) does snapshot → store → `doc.refresh()` → `invalidateLayout()` → `render()`; the new tests assert only `editor.getPageSetup()` and `store.getDocument().pageSetup?.paperSize.name`. Dropping `invalidateLayout()`/`render()` would leave the canvas showing the old paper size and margins with every test still green. I looked for a page-count/layout observable on `EditorAPI` (grepped `getPageCount|pageCount|onPageInfo|_get.*ForTest` in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts) and found none, so this may need a new test hook; noting it as a contained gap rather than a blocker.

samples.summary: 'a paste is one undo step' would also pass if pasteFormat took two snapshots
samples.evidence: The test writes, calls `editor.undo()` once and asserts the target is unstyled. With snapshot-before-write undo semantics, a duplicated `saveSnapshot()` would push two identical pre-write states, so the first undo still restores the unstyled document and the leftover empty undo step goes undetected — the title's claim is not what is asserted. (The snapshot count is genuinely pinned in the bare-TextEditor test in editor-read-only.test.ts, `expect(snapshots).toHaveLength(1)`, so the behaviour is covered elsewhere; only this test's claim is weaker than its name.)

samples.summary: The export-button test file's stated failure-path coverage ('a failure raises a toast rather than an unhandled rejection') is never asserted
samples.evidence: The header comment claims every entry must reach the download through `runExport` 'so a failure raises a toast rather than an unhandled rejection', but the three tests only open the menu and assert filename/MIME on a successful download. No test makes the serializer throw and asserts `toast.error` / no unhandled rejection; `sonner` is not even mocked in this file. Grepped the file for `toast`, `error`, `reject` — none present.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The test at packages/docs/test/view/editor-page-setup.test.ts:116-125 mutates the object returned by getPageSetup() and then asserts toEqual(DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP). DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:745-749) is a mutable module-level object whose paperSize is the shared PAPER_SIZES.LETTER literal (types.ts:737-741, `as const` is type-only, no Object.freeze) and whose margins is a shared literal. setupEditor (test line 73-79) stores a document with no pageSetup, so resolvePageSetup (types.ts:751-758) resolves to DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP. Under the exact aliasing bug this test claims to guard (returning `doc.document.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` instead of the copy at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2917), the two mutations would land on DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP.margins and PAPER_SIZES.LETTER, and the second getPageSetup() would return that same mutated object — so expected and actual mutate in lockstep and the assertion still passes. The same holds for a shallow-copy bug. No copy defect can fail this assertion; the only failure mode left (defaults resolution) is already covered by the test at line 91-95. The contract is documented at editor.ts:125-128 and an alias would let the Page Setup dialog write through into document state, so a vacuous test presented as its coverage is major. The sibling test at line 127-140 uses a real literal oracle, showing the correct pattern. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, unguarded, and vacuous coverage for a changed behavior is squarely in the test-adequacy lane.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The dialog's paper-size Select (docs-page-setup-dialog.tsx:189-215) has an onValueChange handler mapping option name -> PaperSize, plus a CUSTOM sentinel branch (209-213) for a paper size matching no preset. Reading the entire test file, every case only seeds a paper size and asserts it round-trips (lines 74-102, 104-122, 124-137, 149-162) or drives margins/orientation; nothing selects a different paper size, and no test seeds a non-preset size to render 'Custom (name)'. I searched wide for a counterexample elsewhere: DocsPageSetupDialog is imported only by docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:58 and this test; the three toolbar tests never open Page setup (docs-format-painter-toggle.test.tsx:58 only declares a mock pageSetup literal); no playwright/e2e suite exists in the repo; and packages/docs/test/view/editor-page-setup.test.ts:101-146 exercises editor.setPageSetup at the model layer without rendering the dialog, so it cannot catch a broken name->PaperSize mapping. A regression in the select handler (user picks A4, document stays Letter) would ship with a fully green suite — a user-visible, document-affecting gap over the dialog's primary control, which is major under the missing-tests limb of this lens.
